meeting_header: Date: 2025-04-02 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52 min | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Gomez (Redwood CSM), Michael Turner (Acme CISO), Sara Kim (Acme Procurement), Luis Alvarez (Acme Legal), Rina Shah (Acme Platform)
summary: Procurement-focused call to review Redwood MSA and DPA redlines, confirm SLAs and data residency, discuss SOC2/ISO evidence, pricing approval path and onboarding timeline. Action items captured for Redwood to provide security artifacts and redlined contracts; Acme to return redlines and confirm PO/timeline.
topics: DPA: data residency, deletion, audit logs
Pricing approvals and committed capacity vs on-demand
transcript: 00:00 Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we really appreciate you carving out the time. I'm Jordan, AE on the account, with Priya from our SE team and Alex from CSM. 00:18 Michael (Acme): Thanks Jordan, yeah we're ready to walk through the MSA and DPA and get clarity on SLAs and the security artifacts. 00:28 Priya (Redwood SE): Great. Quick agenda — go over the redlines you sent, call out any major sticking points from Redwood perspective, cover SOC2/ISO and KMS details, then pricing and onboarding logistics. Does that work? 00:42 Sara (Acme): Yep, that's the list. We also want to confirm export control language and termination for convenience. 00:51 Jordan (Redwood): Totally, we'll hit those. 01:05 Luis (Acme Legal): Quick note — some of our procurement folks asked for standard vendor insurance and indemnity language to be mirrored from our template. We can point those lines out. 01:20 Priya (Redwood SE): Understood. On indemnities, Redwood tends to propose mutual indemnification with caps that align to the MSA value; happy to show examples. 01:32 Michael (Acme CISO): And on data — we need explicit confirmation that logs will be retained in-region, and that keys are customer-managed or at least customer-controllable. 01:43 Priya (Redwood SE): Yeah, for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM; for Hosted we offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options and can arrange region pinning for logs and data. There's some nuance on instranet vs inference cache — we should call that out. 01:58 Rina (Acme): By 'region pinning' do you mean we could keep data and logs in eu-west-1 only? 02:06 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, we can route to specific regions and also provide audit logs that are stored per region; we'll include retention options in the DPA. 02:18 Jordan (Redwood): Ok let's jump into the MSA PDF you redlined — (screen share noise) — I see a handful of items flagged: SLA uptime, liability cap, termination for convenience, and IP indemnity. 02:38 Luis (Acme Legal): On liability cap we normally push for higher thresholds for security incidents. 02:45 Priya (Redwood SE): I hear that; Redwood's standard is typically a multiple of the last 12 months' fees for liability caps, but for enterprise deals we can negotiate. For security incidents we have incident response commitments and can look at carve-outs. 03:03 Michael (Acme CISO): We also need to see your SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 attestation as part of the vendor evaluation. 03:12 Priya (Redwood SE): Absolutely — we'll share the latest SOC2 Type II attestation and ISO docs. We'll redact PII in the report before sharing if needed, and we'll include a compliance package link. 03:22 Sara (Acme): On pricing — procurement wants to know if committed capacity is required for the SLA or if we can start hosted and then move to dedicated later. 03:33 Jordan (Redwood): Good question. SLA tiers are tied to deployment mode; hosted has best-effort but with strong performance SLAs for paid tiers, dedicated gives stronger, contractual latency and throughput SLAs. You can do a hosted trial and then commit to Dedicated before go-live to get the tighter SLA. 03:50 Rina (Acme Platform): What's the timeline for migrating from hosted to dedicated? 03:55 Priya (Redwood SE): Typically a few weeks for capacity reservation and orchestration, depending on GPU types and model sizing. We'll provide an onboarding plan and timeline. 04:07 Michael (Acme): Regarding DPA — data deletion and export controls are important. Can you confirm deletion guarantees and data access controls for support teams? 04:16 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes — deletion APIs are available, plus we can set retention windows. Support access is auditable via role-based access, and we log all access. We'll include audit log samples. 04:30 Jordan (Redwood): A note on model cache — we do prefix/KV caching to improve latency; that has implications for short-term cached tokens but we treat them as ephemeral and they don't persist beyond configured TTLs. We'll document that in the DPA. 04:45 Luis (Acme Legal): On indemnities related to data, we need language that covers third-party claims due to data leakage. 04:54 Priya (Redwood SE): We can look at language; typically we limit exposure and offer robust security controls plus incident response timelines. 05:05 Jordan (Redwood): Quick pause — Priya, can you confirm the SOC2 artifacts and where you'll put them? 05:12 Priya (Redwood SE): We'll upload the SOC2 Type II to our secure share and also provide a one-pager on encryption options — BYOK and customer-managed KMS, with notes on HSM integration. 05:23 Michael (Acme): Perfect. Sara, do you have any procurement-specific asks? 05:27 Sara (Acme Procurement): We need supplier onboarding forms filled, tax / W9 equivalents, certificate of insurance, and a pricing approval letter. Also need to know payment terms — net30 vs net45. 05:41 Jordan (Redwood): We typically do net30 but can be flexible. We'll include our vendor form and COI. 05:47 Sara (Acme): Also need a clearer schedule of discounts tied to committed monthly spend. 05:53 Jordan (Redwood): We'll include a pricing sheet that shows committed tiers, discounts, and overage rates. 06:01 Rina (Acme): One technical ask — can you support VPC peering and private deployment for sensitive workloads? 06:07 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes — we offer Private deployments with a customer-managed control plane. VPC peering and on-prem options exist; there's an additional onboarding and infra fee for on-prem installs. 06:20 Michael (Acme): Are there any SLA credits? Our security team needs to know remedies for downtime. 06:26 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, the MSA DRAFT includes SLA credits for availability below the agreed percentage. We can propose 99.9% for Dedicated with tiered credits, and 99.5% for hosted paid tiers; open to negotiation in the MSA. 06:41 Luis (Acme Legal): On termination for convenience — we usually ask for a 60-day notice and wind-down assistance. 06:49 Jordan (Redwood): We can accept a 60-day notice and will include migration support in the SOW if that's agreed. 06:57 Michael (Acme): A point on logs — do you allow streaming of audit logs to our SIEM? 07:04 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, we can push audit logs to customer endpoints or S3 in-region; we also support syslog and some SIEM integrations. 07:16 Sara (Acme): Regarding the DPA, data residency — we have EU customer data; we need EU-only processing and subprocessors listed. 07:26 Priya (Redwood SE): We'll provide a list of subprocessors and can commit to EU-only processing for those workloads. Subprocessor addendum and standard contractual clauses can be provided. 07:38 Jordan (Redwood): Ok let's call out the main negotiation points to capture: liability cap, security carve-outs, SLA % for Dedicated, data residency, KMS, indemnity language, and procurement paperwork. 07:52 Alex (Redwood CSM): From onboarding side, we want to flag an initial pilot scope and success criteria — latency targets, QPS, and cost per 1K tokens so procurement can understand unit economics. 08:05 Michael (Acme): On pilots — procurement wants an agreed end-state and a finish line, else they'll stall approvals. 08:12 Jordan (Redwood): Agreed — we'll propose a 30-day pilot with defined SLAs and success metrics and then convert to dedicated if satisfied. 08:23 Sara (Acme): Is there a discount for pilots or is it free? 08:27 Jordan (Redwood): We often offer discounted pilot pricing or time-limited credits. We'll include options in the pricing deck. 08:35 Michael (Acme CISO): I need to confirm two security items: 1) Do you have penetration test results or a PT attestation? 2) How do you handle support access to production-run data? 08:46 Priya (Redwood SE): We'll include a summary of recent penetration tests and a SOC2-level penetration summary; support access is limited, logged, and requires approvals, and we can show the audit trail. 08:58 Luis (Acme Legal): For the DPA, data subject requests — can you support customer's obligations to delete or export data on demand? 09:06 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, we support export and deletion APIs; we can also support data export in specified formats. 09:15 Rina (Acme): Ok, switching to procurement items — Sara, after you get the COI and vendor form from Jordan, what's your internal timeline? 09:22 Sara (Acme Procurement): If legal reviews by next Wednesday and we get redlines by Monday, procurement can aim to finalize PO by the following Friday — so roughly two weeks if everything is smooth. 09:33 Jordan (Redwood): Sounds reasonable. We'll aim to hit those dates. 09:39 Priya (Redwood SE): FYI on technical escalation — we have a runbook and can provide SRE contact model for dedicated customers, including on-call rotation details. 09:50 Michael (Acme CISO): One more on privacy — will you sign our DPA amendments around database encryption and subprocessor constraints? 09:58 Luis (Acme Legal): We'll propose specific language; can Redwood accept some of those redlines? 10:04 Jordan (Redwood): We'll review them; typically we accept many reasonable security redlines and will flag any that materially change our risk profile. 10:12 Priya (Redwood SE): Regarding the quantization/latency tradeoff we mentioned — we can provide recommended quantization profiles per workload to maintain quality while lowering GPU costs; we'll add that to the SOW. 10:26 Rina (Acme): That helps for budgeting. 10:30 Sara (Acme): Ok, payment terms — Jordan, could you note net30 vs net45 options and any early-payment discount? 10:36 Jordan (Redwood): We'll include that in the vendor sheet; typically net30 standard, net45 or extended terms can be negotiated with a slight price adjustment. 10:48 Michael (Acme CISO): Are there any third-party certifications for your hosting infra we should point at? 10:54 Priya (Redwood SE): We use cloud partners with standard certifications; we'll include a list and also provide our SOC2 auditor contact info if needed. 11:05 Luis (Acme Legal): On limitation of liability and IP — we need to ensure our indemnity for IP claims is reasonable if we supply training data. 11:16 Priya (Redwood SE): We'll look at IP clauses; if you supply training data, we can include mutual representations around rights and compliance. 11:24 Jordan (Redwood): We're about halfway through the details; let's make sure action items are clear. Priya — security artifacts; Jordan — contracts and pricing; Acme — redlines and procurement form. 11:40 Priya (Redwood SE): Noted. 11:44 Sara (Acme): Quick question on onboarding — what does success look like operationally? We need runbooks and a knowledge transfer. 11:52 Alex (Redwood CSM): We'll provide runbooks, an onboarding checklist, and a KT schedule. Recommend 2 weeks for internal enablement and 1 week pilot. 12:05 Michael (Acme CISO): For the pilot we want SLAs around latency p95 under X ms and error rate below Y%. 12:12 Jordan (Redwood): We'll work with your platform team to set concrete numbers; typical p95 for target models on Dedicated is in the tens to low hundreds of ms depending on model. 12:25 Rina (Acme): Can you put the model and sequence length assumptions in the SOW? 12:30 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, we'll include model family, sequence lengths, QPS, and expected token mix in the SOW and pricing spreadsheet. 12:45 Luis (Acme Legal): On data retention — what are default retention periods for logs and telemetry? 12:52 Priya (Redwood SE): Default retention is 90 days for detailed request logs, longer aggregated metrics retained 13 months; retention configurable per contract. 13:06 Sara (Acme): If we need longer retention for audit, can that be added? 13:11 Priya (Redwood SE): Absolutely, that's a contract option. 13:17 Jordan (Redwood): Alright let's do a quick recap and next steps — we'll send the redlined MSA & DPA, pricing deck, SOC2 and ISO docs, and vendor forms. Acme will review and return redlines with procurement timeline. 13:36 Michael (Acme): That aligns. 13:40 Jordan (Redwood): Any final questions or items? 13:44 Luis (Acme Legal): We'll add our suggested indemnity language in the redlines. 13:48 Sara (Acme): I'll watch for vendor forms and COI. 13:51 Alex (Redwood CSM): We'll also prepare onboarding calendar options for Apr 10–18. 13:58 Jordan (Redwood): Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with the artifacts. 14:04 Michael (Acme): Thanks all. 51:59 [call end]
